- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.25) and forecast is rising steadily, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.00) and forecast is falling, avoid excessive downward bias — consider slight upward correction.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 80), model often overcorrects — reduce forecast slope by 10–15% in next 5–7 days.  
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of decline after peak), model tends to lag — adjust forecast to align with 2–3 prior true values.  
- If sentiment history shows no clear trend (all 0.00), forecast should not be overly aggressive — use 3–5 day moving average of recent true values as baseline.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates > 5% from forecast mean, check sentiment for hidden momentum — if sentiment is neutral, model may be misaligned with actual volatility.
